liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 other source): Uploader's setlist shows a jam leading into the opener, Hell in a Bucket, at a 7:00 PM listing [5]
- **Drums** (1 review): Mickey played the drums segment using a pair of plastic fly swatters [11]
- **Set Two Intro (Redoing the Grateful Dead's Woodstock performance from 8/16/1969)** (1 review): Weir told the crowd the band tried this sequence at this spot over fifty years earlier, it failed, and they'd try again [9]
- **Easy Wind** (1 review): Played slowed down and loose, with a funky, slap-happy feel that the reviewer loved [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Easy Wnd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]
- **Mama Tried**: back after 34 archived shows (800 days); rare: 7 archived performances [12]
- **High Time**: rare: 13 archived performances [12]
- **Bass**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]
- **Lovelight Reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]

## The recordings

- **deadco2021-08-23.BethelWoodsBethelNY** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 192 min [1]
- **DeadCo2021-08-23.litz.schoepsMK41v.flac24**: source not stated; 21 songs; 194 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [2]
- **deadco2021-08-23.153138.akg.c63.suraci.flac16**: source not stated; 1 songs; 193 min [5]
- **deadco2021-08-23.153199.nak700.jtny.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 192 min [3]

## Around the show

- The crowd went wild at Weir's introduction to the second set, the Woodstock redo [11]
- Lineup listed is Weir, Mayer and Burbridge; an asterisk marks Oteil as playing only during Bass Space [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **deadco2021-08-23.BethelWoodsBethelNY**: taped by JT/NY; transferred by JT/NY; source: Aud > Nakamichi CM700's w 701 Caps > GakCables > Lunatec V3 > Sound Devices 722 @ 24/96 [1]. Also: Audience recording: Nakamichi CM700 mics with 701 capsules, GakCables, Lunatec V3, Sound Devices 722 at 24/96; edited in Sound Forge Pro 13, converted to FLAC [1]
- **DeadCo2021-08-23.litz.schoepsMK41v.flac24**: taped by Keith Litzenberger; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Schoeps MK41v's>Schoeps KCY250/5i>Baby Nbox>Sony PCM-A10 [2]. Also: Schoeps MK41v mics into KCY250/5i, Baby Nbox and Sony PCM-A10 at 24/96; Sound Forge Pro 15 fades, FLAC via Trader's Little Helper [2]
- **deadco2021-08-23.153138.akg.c63.suraci.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: AKG CK63>Naiant Active Cables>Sound Devices 722 [5]. Also: Taper Tony Suraci used AKG CK63 mics, Naiant active cables and a Sound Devices 722, with a CF card transfer through Adobe Audition 3.0 to 24-bit FLAC [5]
- **deadco2021-08-23.153199.nak700.jtny.flac16**: taped by jtny; transferred by jtny; source: Nakamichi CM700's w 701 Caps > GakCables > Lunatec V3 > Sound Devices 722 @ 24/96 [3]
